coverage.target: No infrastructure is involved: the pure, frozen marker rule is a property of site/src/lib/navigation.ts, enforced by the unit's unit and property tests, and the build has no runtime that could read I/O.

No infrastructure change: U4 adds no asset, process, request or pipeline stage, so the deployed tree keeps the existing mirror (rsync -a --delete of site/dist/ to the web root). The weight budget is measured on the built tree by the Build and Test stage.

No infrastructure is involved: the build-time budget (median of 3 fixture builds at or below 3.81 s against the recorded 3.63 s) is measured by the Build and Test stage on the local fixture pair, and the nightly Jenkins Build Site stage grades nothing - it runs one build over the real vault's content. U4 adds no build step, worker or cache.

Jenkins Build Site gate: a failed Astro build stops the run before the Deploy stage, so an invalid navigation model never reaches the web root; the static server and the Cloudflare Tunnel serve only a tree that was built successfully.
No infrastructure is involved: the marker contract and the axe matrix are a property of the served HTML, checked by the Playwright HIG suite on the locally built site.
No infrastructure is involved: the 44 px target and the 52 px sheet row are CSS values in the existing chrome stylesheet served from the same origin.

The single existing origin: Cloudflare Tunnel `obsidian-blog` (launchd `dev.rvnnt.tunnel`) publishes the static server `dev.rvnnt.blog` on 127.0.0.1:8080. U4 adds no external font, script, image or stylesheet, so the deployed tree keeps one origin.
No infrastructure is involved: the navigation works with JavaScript off because the sheet is static HTML in the built tree; the check runs in the local crossunit browser project.
Jenkins Verify stage: `cargo test --release` plus `npm run test:unit && npm run test:pbt` fail the nightly run before Deploy, so the existing suites stay green on every change that ships.
